Police may detain you for at most twenty‑four hours after an arrest without a warrant, unless a magistrate issues a special order under section 167.

citations.quote: shall not, in the absence of a special order of a Magistrate under section 167, exceed twenty-four hours exclusive of the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the Magistrate's Court.

Investigation is normally carried out by the police. Specifically, any officer in charge of a police‑station may, without a magistrate’s order, investigate a cognizable case. A magistrate may also direct an investigation or appoint a subordinate magistrate to do so.

citations.quote: Any officer in charge of a police-station may, without the order of a Magistrate, investigate any cognizable case which a Court having jurisdiction over the local area within the limits of such station would have power to inquire into or try under the provisions of Chapter XV relating to the place of inquiry or trial.

Such Magistrate, on receiving such report, may direct an investigation or, if he thinks fit, at once proceed, or depute any Magistrate subordinate to him to proceed, to hold a preliminary inquiry into, or otherwise to dispose of, the case in manner provided in this Code.

text: Yes. Under section 89 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the Court may restore attached property (or the net proceeds of a sale) to a person who, within two years of the attachment, appears before the Court, shows that he did not abscond or conceal himself to avoid execution of the warrant and was unable to attend the proclamation, and then the property shall be delivered to him after costs are satisfied.

citations.quote: If, within two years from the date of the attachment any person whose property is or has been at the disposal of the Government, under sub-section (7) of section 88, appears voluntarily ... and proves ... that he did not abscond or conceal himself for the purpose of avoiding execution of the warrant, ... such property ... shall, after satisfying thereout all costs incurred in consequence of the attachment, be delivered to him.
